paper_metadata.title: Strong and ductile CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy microfibers at ambient and cryogenic temperatures

evidence.quote: a heterogeneous gradient structure was introduced into CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) microfibers via thermomechanical processing.

evidence.quote: An equimolar CoCrFeNi HEA ingot was fabricated using vacuum induction melting in argon atmosphere from pure Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni metals with purities higher than 99.9 wt% and was remelted at least four times to ensure compositional homogeneity.
The HEA rod was homogenized by annealing at 1473 K for 24 h.
The rod was hot-rotary to 8 mm in diameter along the longitudinal direction at 1173 K, and then hot-drawn to 1 mm.

parameters.deformation: ~10% cross-sectional area reduction per pass; final diameter ~70 μm

evidence.quote: Subsequently, the rod was subjected to multi-pass cold-drawing at ambient temperatures. After each drawing step, the cross-sectional area was reduced by ~ 10% and thermal annealing was employed at 1173 K for 1 h. Finally, the initial microfibers with a diameter of ~ 70 μ m was obtained.
After each drawing step, the cross-sectional area was reduced by ~ 10% and thermal annealing was employed at 1173 K for 1 h.
To achieve gradient heterogeneous microstructure with controllable grain sizes, the cold-drawn CoCrFeNi microfibers were heat treated at 1023 K for 1 h in a vacuum furnace.
The XRD pattern only shows single-phase FCC peaks ( Fig. 2 c), indicating a single-phase FCC solid solution structure for the annealed HEA microfiber.
The corresponding dark-field image ( Fig. 1 b) further confirms the existence of elongated twin lamellae with an average width of 40 ± 15 nm.
The bottom right SAED pattern reveals the presence of nano-grains at specific spots (region II) because of the accumulated strain.
The typical bright field TEM image ( Fig. 1 a) shows a large number of the dislocations and deformation twins (DTs)
A typical bright-field TEM image ( Fig. 2 h) shows that the annealed microfibers possess many dislocations.
Some annealing twins are also observed, as also verified by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern ( Fig. 2 i).
The grain size and shape exhibit a gradient from the surface to the center of the microfiber
The grain size ranges from 0.25 to 6 μ m with a mean value of 1.9 ± 0.3 μ m ( Fig. 2 e).
The average GND densities are calculated to be 2.59 × 10^15 m^2 and 7.35 × 10^15 m^2 for the 293 K-sample and 150 K-sample, respectively.

The DF image ( Fig. 7 c) corresponding to Fig. 7 b reveals that the average twin width is 32 nm
we also observed a special lamellar structure in the 150 K sample, composed of FCC matrix, twin, and HCP nanolayers, as shown in Fig. 7 d. Fig. 7 e shows the HCP stacking with four atomic layers.
